one_liner: Embedded, eventually consistent Rust key-value store for ML features that serves reads in-process instead of calling a remote Redis.
what_it_does: IKV keeps a local replica of a data partition inside each application process: a Rust core, loaded as a native library over JNI (Java), cgo (Go) or cffi (Python), answers get(primary key, field name) lookups with no network call. Writes go through a separate writer client to a data plane (gRPC gateway, Kafka, S3 base-index snapshots), which fans them out to every reader within milliseconds. Records are schemaless documents with typed fields (int32/int64/float32/float64/bool/string/bytes), and reads are single or multi-get by key and field. It has no Redis protocol, commands, TTLs or read-after-write guarantee.
how_it_is_fast: Reads never leave the process. The primary key is hashed with fxhash to one of 16 RwLock-guarded segments. There, an in-memory std HashMap maps the key to a per-field vector of offsets, and the value is sliced out of an append-only memory-mapped file (2-byte type tag, then fixed-width bytes or a varint length). When data exceeds RAM it spills through the OS page cache, which keeps skewed (Zipfian) reads on local SSD under a millisecond on average. Writes are applied asynchronously by a background Kafka consumer, so the read path pays nothing for replication or consensus.
when_to_use: Read-heavy online ML feature serving (recommendation, search, ranking), where every app host can hold its partition locally and a few milliseconds of staleness is fine.
Per-lookup budgets in single-digit microseconds that a same-AZ network round trip (about 300 us to ElastiCache in the vendor's test) cannot meet.
Feature sets 2-4x larger than RAM with skewed access, on hosts with local NVMe. The vendor measured avg 53 us (1:2) and 118 us (1:4 memory:data) with sub-millisecond p99.
Java, Go or Python services that would otherwise put a remote Redis or DynamoDB in front of static or slowly changing features.
As an MIT-licensed reference design for an embedded read replica: hash index, append-only mmap and stream replay from a snapshot plus Kafka.
when_not_to_use: You need read-after-write consistency, atomic updates, TTL or eviction, or Redis data structures. IKV has none of these; reads are eventually consistent.

You cannot run its data plane. The hosted IKV Cloud is gone, self-hosting is still marked 'coming soon' in the README, and the ikv-cloud code expects Kafka, S3 and a DynamoDB-backed Java gateway with no setup docs.

Memory is tight or the fleet is large. Every reader holds the whole key-to-offset hash table on heap and a full copy of its partition. Old values are only reclaimed by an offline index-build compaction.
Tail latency matters on tiered data: at 1:4 memory:data, IKV's p99 was 747.65 us against 348.88 us for in-memory single-shard Redis.

You want production maturity or a Rust API. It stopped at v0.0.36, nearly all commits are by one developer, and the core crate is built only as a cdylib behind C/JNI entry points, with no Rust-facing API.

integration.dependencies: Core (Rust): rdkafka (librdkafka with vendored OpenSSL), tokio, aws-sdk-s3, memmap2, protobuf, jni, fxhash, flate2/tar. Runtime: a Kafka topic per store, an S3 bucket for base-index snapshots, and a gRPC gateway for config and writes. Python SDK: boto3, cffi, grpcio, protobuf.
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 2021 edition (MSRV not documented); Python SDK requires Python 3.8+; Go and Java minimums not documented.
integration.platforms: The SDK loaders only know prebuilt binaries for linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64 and macOS aarch64 (no Windows, no Intel Mac). 64-bit only: the offset table uses usize and is commented as 32-bit incompatible. The prebuilt binary bucket no longer exists, so you must build from source.
integration.thread_safety: One reader handle is shared across threads. Lookups take read locks on the schema and on one of 16 RwLock segments. A background Kafka consumer thread takes per-segment write locks to apply each write.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false. It is a different architecture and API: typed document/field getters in the Java/Go/Python SDKs, a separate writer that goes through the data plane, eventual consistency, and no Redis protocol.

gotchas: The 'no network calls' claim covers steady-state reads only. Opening a reader fetches config over gRPC from gateway.inlined.io, may download a base-index tarball from S3 (region hard-coded to us-west-2), and blocks until its Kafka partition is consumed to the high watermark. All vendor endpoints are now dead, so readers cannot start without code changes or a self-hosted data plane.

Supply-chain risk: the Go and Python SDKs list a public S3 bucket named ikv-binaries, download the highest-versioned libikv from it, and dlopen it. That bucket now returns NoSuchBucket, so anyone who re-creates the name could serve the code the SDKs load. Pin and build your own binary. Also, the README's inlined.io links now redirect to an unrelated site flagged as potentially malicious.

The Kafka consumer sets enable.ssl.certificate.verification=false while it authenticates with the account passkey over SASL/SCRAM. In a self-hosted setup, override this with the kafkaprop_ config prefix.

Durability and robustness are thin. mmap.flush() is commented out ('TODO(critical): this fails on macos'), so value bytes are synced only when the OS writes pages back. The JNI and C entry points unwrap() or expect() on inputs and config. A comment warns that a panic in the consumer thread is not surfaced.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Garnet, Dragonfly, KeyDB and Pogocache are shared network servers benchmarked on server throughput against Redis, and Caffeine is an in-process JVM heap cache you fill yourself. Pick IKV only if you want every app host to hold a stream-synced, disk-spillable read replica of a feature dataset and will run and maintain its Kafka/S3 data plane yourself. Otherwise a sibling is the safer choice.
verified_claims_summary: In the in-memory test, 16 Java threads read from IKV embedded in a c5.4xlarge and, through JedisCluster HGET, from a 16-shard ElastiCache Redis 7.1 cluster (cache.r5.xlarge) in the same AZ, on 1M docs with three 50 B fields. IKV averaged about 3 us (p99 about 5-6 us) versus about 320 us (p99 about 515-530 us) for Redis at 25K-100K QPS, and it also held 1M and 3M QPS. The tiered test (c5d.4xlarge local SSD, Zipfian, 6000 B docs, 16 IKV threads vs 1 Redis thread, different dataset sizes per system) gave IKV avg 118 us / p99 748 us at 1:4 memory:data, versus avg 225 / p99 349 us for in-memory single-shard Redis. No CPU model, compiler or flags were given, and most of the gap is the removed network hop.
status_note: The project has been stale since v0.0.36 (2024-05-14) and is effectively orphaned. As of 2026-09-26, inlined.io redirects to an unrelated flagged site, docs.inlined.io and gateway.inlined.io do not resolve, and the SDKs' binary bucket is gone. Using it now means building libikv from source and self-hosting or patching out the data plane, though the MIT-licensed Rust index is small enough to study or vendor.
